question: Should OpenClaw core adopt repeatable ordered config layers as a supported Gateway startup contract with read-only lifetime semantics?
rationale: This introduces a public CLI and configuration lifecycle mode that intentionally disables writes, reload, bootstrap, and migration behavior; source correctness alone cannot establish that permanent product boundary.

options.title: Sponsor After Repair
options.body: Approve the direction contingent on path-scoped write ownership, coexistence coverage, and explicit lifecycle documentation.

options.title: Keep In RFC
options.body: Pause implementation until https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/34 settles ownership, precedence, and lifecycle semantics.

options.title: Decline Core Surface
options.body: Keep configuration composition in managed-host launchers instead of adding another OpenClaw core startup mode.

recommendation.title: Sponsor After Repair
recommendation.body: Approve the direction contingent on path-scoped write ownership, coexistence coverage, and explicit lifecycle documentation.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the broadest recent history across the central config I/O and Gateway startup contracts affected by the decision.
